accuracy.reason: All eight objectives are accurate and bounded: asynchronous acceptance, actor/acknowledgement boundaries, duplicate-safe effects, finite retry/isolation, effect order, finite capacity, independent log groups and synchronous dependency decisions. Primary sources support critical claims; no universal exactly-once or durability guarantee is invented.

evidence.quote: These acknowledgements cover different boundaries. Neither makes a broker operation atomic with a database write or proves an arbitrary business effect succeeded.
That transaction protects its database effects. It does not make an external email or payment atomic, or turn delivery into a universal exactly-once guarantee.
Ordering is per partition, not global across all partitions. Retained history and offsets do not by themselves make external effects exactly once.

mechanisms.reason: The reader can trace publish/confirm/effect/acknowledge, both crash windows, an atomic unique-ID/effect transaction, delayed retries and inspection, concurrent overwrite and per-ID serialization, arrival-minus-completion backlog, and offset-based replay. Declared transactions/unique constraints and arithmetic suffice.

evidence.quote: In one database transaction, insert that ID into a durable processed-jobs table with a unique constraint and apply the receipt changes. Commit both or neither. A duplicate ID skips the effect. A separate check followed by a write can race or crash between steps.
Serialize effects per receipt ID: keep later updates waiting while an earlier one runs or retries. Different receipts can still run in parallel. A busy receipt becomes a throughput bottleneck.
If 100 receipt jobs arrive each second and 70 finish, unfinished work grows by 30 jobs per second. Watch backlog and oldest-job age: a growing wait can violate the promise to the client.

coherence.reason: Receipt generation connects all eight cards. Completion precedes acknowledgements, redelivery precedes retry/replay, and concurrency precedes capacity. The actor diagram preserves acknowledgement boundaries; queue/log diagram distinguishes divided work from independent groups without claiming global order. Layout is not assessed.

evidence.quote: The client checks that ID for pending, ready, or failed status. Only ready means the receipt can be used; an accepted response is not the receipt.
Receives the message, saves the receipt and ready status, then acknowledges processing to the broker. A consumer acknowledgement lets the broker retire that delivery.

If receipts and analytics each need every purchase event, a retained log such as Kafka supports separate consumer groups. A partition is an ordered slice of the log. Each group tracks its own position, called an offset, for each partition. Workers within a group share the partitions.

decisions.reason: Explains defer versus wait, durable duplicate protection, transient versus persistent recovery, per-entity ordering cost, bounded admission/downstream concurrency, and queue versus retained log. Final card connects synchronous authorization to its required result and lists concrete operating costs.

evidence.quote: Healthy jobs can continue. Before deliberately replaying a failed job, fix its cause and check whether an earlier attempt already applied an effect. Replay still needs duplicate safety.
More workers help when workers are the bottleneck and downstream services have spare capacity. If the database is already saturated, more workers increase contention instead.
Authorization must finish before showing a private receipt. Queueing the decision and granting access immediately would use a result we do not yet have.
The tradeoff includes operating the broker and workers, tracking status, handling duplicates and retries, and watching backlog. A queue does not solve sustained overload.

clarity.reason: Producer, broker, worker, idempotency, dead-letter purpose, serialization, backpressure, partition and offset receive concrete explanations before required application. The same example and explicit limits keep the required reasoning accessible without undeclared messaging knowledge.

evidence.quote: Holds work for consumers. A publisher confirmation means broker acceptance under the configured durability rules, not a completed receipt.
Repeating the same operation has the same effect as doing it once. Reuse a stable business-operation ID across retries, not a new ID per attempt.

sourceChecks.claim: Microsoft asynchronous-request-reply body separates fast 202 acceptance from status polling and completed results; it describes long work and additional notification complexity.

RabbitMQ explicitly says publisher confirms and consumer acknowledgements are independent boundaries; confirms cover publisher/broker interactions while consumer acknowledgements mark processed deliveries for deletion. Manual unacknowledged work is requeued on failure.

AWS substantive idempotency body requires stable request IDs and ACID token-plus-mutation recording, avoiding either mutation or record alone. RabbitMQ requeue-on-consumer-failure supports the crash window; neither implies atomic external effects.

Microsoft Retry body distinguishes transient and permanent failures, increasing delays/finite attempts, overload risk and idempotency. Linked lesson Competing Consumers describes poison-message capture and dead-letter thresholds, supporting isolation rather than repair.

Microsoft Competing Consumers body warns about ordering and dependent tasks and links per-session sequencing. Concurrent workers permit the illustrated completion inversion; serial effects per entity prevent overtaking while limiting that entity throughput.

Microsoft load-leveling body expressly warns that unconstrained consumers move overload downstream, producers above consumer rate grow queue/latency, and queues have size and retention limits; it recommends safe consumer bounds and producer shedding.

Kafka design body specifies ordered partitions, one consumer per partition in each group, checkpointed offsets and rewind. Retention/compaction is separate from progress. External exactly-once output needs coordination with the destination rather than offsets alone.

Microsoft asynchronous pattern separates acknowledgement/status from result; Competing Consumers identifies workloads requiring completed synchronous results as unsuitable. Thus authorization cannot grant access from an unfinished queued decision, while deferred receipts require tracked completion/failure.
